title: Predictive KV slot sharding and fragmentation attenuation playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: reduce long-term KV cache fragmentation and tail memory amplification while preserving latency SLOs for continuous batching. We will design and implement a predictive sharding strategy for KV slots that groups slots by observed lifetime and access hotness, combined with opportunistic micro-compaction windows and lazy slot migration to minimize disruptive memcpy spikes on GPU. The approach must integrate with the continuous-batching scheduler so TTLs and batching-aligned lifetimes are respected, and should provide telemetry hooks for automated tuning and rollback.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end prototype demonstrates >=25% reduction in allocatable fragmentation on 4 GPU nodes running mixed production traces without increasing p99 latency by >5%. 2) New telemetry surfaces per-shard fragmentation, slot churn, and micro-compaction CPU/GPU cost. 3) Graceful fallback to existing allocation policy when compaction budget exceeded. 4) Documented rollout plan, perf tests, and a canary run on dedicated pool.
risks:
- Background compaction may introduce transient latency spikes if scheduled poorly.
- Incorrect lifetime prediction could increase cross-shard migrations and worsen fragmentation.
- Integration complexity with continuous batching scheduler may create ordering hazards for KV entries tied to in-flight batched requests.
- Telemetry noise from synthetic workloads could mislead autotuning rules.
implementation_notes:
High-level plan:
1) Telemetry baseline: capture per-request KV insert lifetime, read frequency, sequence-length conditioned histograms, and GPU free-run utilization windows.
2) Offline analysis: compute quantile-based lifetime buckets (short/medium/long) and hotness scores; use this to pick shard sizes and target slot granularity.
3) Runtime: implement 'predictive shard table' that maps model+request-pattern signatures to shard id; allocator attempts in-shard placement first, otherwise places in a burst-reserve bucket.
4) Micro-compaction: small-window compaction tasks run when GPU SM utilization < threshold and KV defrag metric exceeds threshold; compaction moves slots within same lifetime bucket to contiguous regions using async memcpy and KV indirection to avoid prolonged locks.
5) Lazy migration: for hot entries that need relocation, insert an indirection entry and migrate on next read to amortize cost.
6) Batching integration: expose per-batch 'slot-affinity' hint so sequence-aligned requests allocate in same shard when possible; ensure rollback safety with canary flag.
7) Safety: global compaction budget, per-GPU rate limits, and fast disable flag for SRE.
8) Tests: unit allocator tests, GPU mem-sim harness, end-to-end with production trace replay and CI perf gates.

2026-02-20 - Telemetry PR merged: added per-insert lifetime stamp + sequence-length tag. Observed heavy bi-modal lifetime distribution in chat workloads (short prompts vs long context sessions).

2026-02-23 - Design sync: decided on 'burst-reserve' strategy to avoid immediate large allocations that fragment primary shards; Marco to prototype allocator changes in runtime/allocators/slot_shard.cc.

2026-02-25 - Perf note: initial micro-compaction prototype on a dev node reduced free-run fragmentation metric by 18% but produced 40ms memcpy spikes under naive scheduling. Need async memcpy + stricter scheduling.

2026-02-28 - Code review feedback: PR requests tighter invariants around indirection table updates and stronger unit tests for race conditions during migration. Added two follow-ups: ENG-456701 (indirection safety tests) and ENG-456702 (compaction scheduler tuning).
